title: Regularization and supersymmetry-restoring counterterms in supersymmetric QCD
claim: One-loop SUSY-restoring counterterms in SQCD: compares DREG with anticommuting gamma5 (theta_DReg = 1) and DRED (theta_DReg = 0). DREG needs finite non-symmetric counterterms: in the gluon/gluino SUSY transformations -(alpha_s C(A)/4 pi)(1/3) theta_DReg (eq. 28), quark/squark SUSY transformations -(alpha_s C(F)/4 pi)(1/2) theta_DReg (eq. 35), gluino-quark-squark vertex (alpha_s/4 pi)(2/3 C(A) - 1/2 C(F)) theta_DReg (eqs. 42-43); gauge interactions need none (eq. 46); gluon-gluino-gluino none (eq. 52). DRED needs no non-symmetric counterterms at one loop.
theory: SQCD (Wess-Zumino gauge, soft breaking via auxiliary multiplet)
scheme: DREG with anticommuting gamma5 (not BMHV); DRED.
symmetry_argument: ST identity with constant SUSY/translation ghosts; uniqueness of counterterms requires the SUSY-algebra identities, not only Ward identities (Sec. 3.2).

proved: One-loop SUSY-restoring counterterms in DREG (values above); none needed in DRED for the considered trilinear interactions and SUSY-transformation operators.
assumed: Both DREG with anticommuting gamma5 and DRED are inconsistent beyond one loop but differ from a consistent scheme by local counterterms (App. C, footnote 9).

red_flags: Uses anticommuting gamma5 in DREG, so it is not a BMHV analysis; R-invariance is preserved by the regularization (Sec. 3.4), which BMHV would break (see S3.07).
notes: Recorded under S3 only to document the gamma5 treatment (answer to the brief: not BMHV).
